ZBoard is a minimal, extensible panel for users, subscriptions, nodes and system services. This RC corrects subscription lifecycle and commerce flows, restores administration controls and improves operational statistics while preserving existing capabilities.

## Changes

- Organize default administration menus around user, subscription, node and service modules. Upgrade only untouched default placements; preserve administrator presentation edits, stable menu IDs and plugin attachments. Keep existing provider, DNS and certificate capabilities available.
- Unify direct protocols and forward entries in the paged node-protocol inventory, with parent relationships, deployment mode, server presence, addresses, access groups and clearly attributed parent traffic statistics. Connect product details to their access group and the group's authorized services.
- Register externally operated forwarding addresses without requiring a panel-managed forwarding server. Existing managed forwarding retains its deployment behavior. Granting only a forward entry now issues its parent protocol credential while delivering only the authorized forwarding address; direct addresses require their own membership. Entry removal and membership changes reconcile parent credentials and surviving node publications.
- Use bounded server-side search, paging and selection snapshots for both direct and forwarding group members, including page inversion. Fix access-group filters reaching the API, avoid loading all entry memberships for paged group summaries, and use the SQLite reporting connection for inventory reads.

- Fix MySQL startup failures `1419` followed by `1050` in hourly traffic migration 0024. Recover committed partial tables/indexes and rebuild aggregates from the untouched ledger without enabling function trust or granting SUPER. Migration 0025 replaces MySQL triggers with atomic application writes; existing trigger installations also upgrade without double counting.

- Show only operations backed by published products and saleable SKUs. Product and SKU deletion archives catalog entries while preserving historical order snapshots.
- Allow an unexpired timed subscription to change plans after its cycle traffic is exhausted, including when no reset SKU exists. Exhausted traffic has zero transferable value. Payment replaces the cycle quota with the target plan quota, retains consumed traffic and preserves expiry; it does not reset usage or append another billing period.
- Lock the time-based credit when creating a plan-change order, so waiting for payment alone does not invalidate the agreed price. Settlement still rejects exhausted credit caused by additional consumption, refunds, source changes, expiry or a new reset cycle.
- Sell traffic resets through a configured one-time reset SKU and order. Pending or canceled orders do not restore quota; settlement authorization and repeat-safe fulfillment remain mandatory. A paid reset restores the subscription's base cycle quota without extending expiry or moving the next scheduled reset.
- Stop ended services immediately. Renewable subscriptions retain their instance for seven days and can recover through paid renewal during that window. Nonrenewable single-use services are cleaned up at expiry or exhaustion; historical orders retain their terminal status and final quota/usage. Late payment cannot recreate a cleaned target.
- Preserve the previous period's terminal order history when renewing within the grace window, even before the expiry worker runs. The successful recovery order shows the restored service; future plan-change credit includes only the new paid period.
- Repair existing fixed-quota subscriptions sold with timed validity rather than a `once` billing unit. Exhausted nonrenewable services disappear from current-service lists and active counts before retirement; orders retain their final state. Align ranking card padding, names, comparisons, values and period controls across desktop and mobile.
- Keep monthly subscriptions visible when current-cycle traffic is exhausted. Display available purchase operations from the actual catalog rather than offering unusable reset or renewal buttons.
- Apply administrator quota changes to the latest locked subscription, changing only submitted fields. Preserve original traffic records and reasoned before/after audit history with idempotent retries.
- Unify menu editing and input interactions, support checkbox deselection and reduce redundant SKU configuration. Preset billing periods retain custom values. Provide contextual user/order/subscription links, advanced filters, collapsed quota editing and node setup guidance.
- Add timezone-aware revenue comparisons, traffic trends and node/user rankings. Maintain hourly traffic aggregates transactionally and use bounded ledger reads for partial hours, reducing long-window reporting work. Dashboard requests load independently and cancel obsolete requests.
- Preserve plugin management, optional integrations and existing node publication capabilities. Plugin filters use shared controls and actual execution state.

## Node protocol and task management updates

- Show server presence, endpoint address and port, enabled state, active users and connections, and traffic together in the node-protocol list. Edit listener ports in the service editor; adjust subscription display order by dragging whole rows in the list.
- Treat configuration publication as a task observation rather than proof that a protocol is usable. Pending, running and failed node publication requests appear from the live queue even when older deployment logs have been retained or removed.
- Let administrators reset a protocol's displayed traffic measurement period with a reason. Migration `0028_protocol_endpoint_usage_resets` stores the new baseline and audit record; the original usage ledger and subscription accounting remain intact.
- List handlers registered in the current application instance independently of execution-statistics reads. Compact the background-task overview and make long queue errors available on demand; narrow screens show execution history as records with the relevant actions.

## Connector lock contention fix

Buffered `flow.updated` and `stats.sampled` requests acknowledge after durable spool append and enqueue their node receipt without waiting for a node metadata write. The existing consumer coalesces receipts, skips locked MySQL node rows, bounds connection-pool waits and retries later. Credentials are revalidated under the row lock; an old receipt cannot overwrite a newer stopped state.

Accounting writes node statistics after flow settlement within the same transaction. MySQL consumer transactions are capped at 128 events with continuing backlog drain, preserving atomic accounting, checkpoints and replay idempotency. No additional migration is required for this fix.

Real MySQL regressions hold node/subscription locks, send concurrent authenticated HTTP receipts through the file spool, exhaust the connection pool, revoke credentials and inject node-statistics failures. They verify durable acceptance, post-contention recovery, rollback and replay. These tests also run in the MySQL CI job. Production lock holders and deployment recovery still require live verification.

## Updating

Back up the database, deployment configuration, encryption keys, plugin packages and managed rules. Use this exact RC image tag. Preserve the previous image and database backup for rollback.

This RC adds migrations `0022_catalog_archive`, `0023_subscription_lifecycle`, `0024_traffic_usage_hourly`, `0025_traffic_hourly_application`, `0026_fixed_quota_lifecycle`, `0027_external_forward_entries` and `0028_protocol_endpoint_usage_resets` for MySQL and SQLite. SQLite retains its existing transaction-local triggers; 0025 records an engine-specific no-op. The MySQL traffic migration repairs partial 0024 installations automatically and backfills historical records; run one instance with `-migrate-only` while other application writers are stopped, then start application instances after migration completes. Do not race MySQL DDL between instances or run old and new writers together. Do not delete the original traffic ledger, manually mark migration 0024 complete, or enable global function trust to work around this failure. An existing installation with old triggers needs its usual schema-level TRIGGER permission to remove them; no SUPER privilege is required. Rolling back this change requires the pre-upgrade database snapshot along with the previous binary, because the previous MySQL binary depends on the removed triggers. Preserve the existing credential encryption key.

Migration 0027 adds forwarding deployment mode and permits external entries without a forwarding-server reference; existing entries remain managed. Preserve the pre-upgrade database snapshot when rolling back to a version that assumes every entry has a server.

Configure a published traffic-reset SKU, its price and the reset operation to offer paid resets. A subscription's automatic reset schedule and audited administrator adjustments remain separate from customer reset purchases. Payment providers remain optional plugins.

Local backend tests and vet, frontend tests, type checking, production builds and OpenAPI validation are checked before tagging. Publication does not migrate or deploy an existing installation; production database, node recovery and live browser behavior still require verification after upgrade.
